units.text: INT. ART RESTORATION LAB - NIGHT
White light over an easel.
Solvent fumes.
A large Dutch still life lies on the table, its lower third scraped to the ground layer.
CELESTE DUMAS, 40s, conservator, in white gloves and a magnifying visor, works a cotton swab along a patch of ochre with the calm of someone defusing a bomb.
IVO, 30s, her assistant, photographs each stroke.
SABINE, 20s, a student, holds a lamp so steady it seems to be part of her arm.
There's something under the lemon.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: Under?
units.name: IVO

units.text: It's a signature.
units.name: SABINE

units.text: It's not the artist's.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: Whose?
units.name: IVO

units.text: Look at the letters. They're pressed in from behind.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: The swab pauses.
Under the lemon, a ghostly mark appears, a thin cross-hatched initial.
Ivo steps closer, his camera dropping.
That's the Fenwick stamp.
units.name: IVO

units.text: The forgery ring?
units.name: SABINE

units.text: Not a forgery. A transfer. The original is under this one.
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: The door at the end of the lab clicks open.
All three look up.
ANTON KOLOSOV, 50s, in a long coat dusted with rain, stands in the doorway holding a key card in one hand and a thin black briefcase in the other.
Don't touch the lemon.
units.name: KOLOSOV

units.text: Mr. Kolosov. How did you get in?
units.name: CELESTE

units.text: I paid for the lock.
units.name: KOLOSOV

units.text: You were told the lab is closed.
units.name: IVO

units.text: And I was told this painting was clean. We are all disappointed tonight.
units.name: KOLOSOV

units.text: Sabine lowers the lamp.
Light slides off the canvas and across the floor, across his shoes.
Celeste straightens, and her hand, quietly, finds the solvent bottle.
